extracted.intended_audience: authors, referees, and editors participating in SciPost journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and standards for SciPost's open 'peer-witnessed refereeing' process used by its overlay journals (preprints via arXiv; refereeing, publication, and post-publication commenting managed by SciPost). Covers procedural requirements, report practices, acceptance criteria, quality expectations, and transparency commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlay journal model (preprint via arXiv; SciPost manages refereeing/publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: SciPost operates as an overlay journal: preprint handling and circulation occurs through arXiv; SciPost provides the remainder of the publication process — peer refereeing through publication and post-publication commenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should manage preprint submission/availability via arXiv; SciPost's role starts with editorial pickup and runs through refereeing, decision, publication, and post-publication discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial processing pickup by a Fellow of an Editorial College
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted manuscripts must be picked up for editorial processing by one of the Fellows of an Editorial College.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a procedural gate: a manuscript is handled only after a Fellow takes it on for editorial processing (implies papers require assignment to an appropriate Fellow to enter the refereeing workflow).

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-witnessed refereeing procedure (report visibility and signing options)
rubrics_metrics.description: SciPost uses an open procedure known as peer-witnessed refereeing. Reports on submissions are anonymous by default; anonymity can be waived if the contributor wishes; SciPost encourages referees to sign their reports; all reports become publicly visible with the published paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees may choose anonymity or to sign; regardless, reports are part of the public record once the paper is published. The process aims to combine openness with optional reviewer privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality standard: extremely stringent refereeing
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts undergo 'extremely stringent peer-witnessed refereeing' guaranteeing that papers published in SciPost Journals meet the highest possible academic standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SciPost asserts a high bar for scientific quality; referees and editors are expected to apply rigorous standards across methodological, conceptual, and presentation aspects of submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance criterion: originality and novelty of contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality and novelty of contribution — the manuscript should present original work and novel results or insights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers are evaluated on whether they add new knowledge or perspectives beyond existing literature; lack of novelty is a ground for rejection or major revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance criterion: significance of advance to the field
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance of advance to the field — the work should represent a meaningful advance for its research area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators consider the importance and likely impact of the findings on the discipline; incremental or trivial advances may not meet this bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance criterion: validity of the research and arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Validity of the research and arguments — the methods, results, analyses, and conclusions should be sound and well-supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees must assess methodological rigor, correctness of reasoning, reproducibility where applicable, and whether conclusions follow from evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance criterion: quality of writing and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of writing and presentation — the manuscript must be clearly written and well-presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity, organization, completeness of exposition, quality of figures/tables, and overall readability are considered; poor presentation can impede acceptance even for valid results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency: public availability of manuscript, reports, responses, and decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: SciPost makes the submitted manuscript, all reports (anonymous or signed), author responses, and editor decisions publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This openness is intended to foster accountability and quality in refereeing. Authors and referees should expect that these elements will be part of the public record for published papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication commenting
rubrics_metrics.description: SciPost offers post-publication commenting as part of its publication process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After publication, the community can engage in discussion/commenting on papers hosted by SciPost, contributing to ongoing scrutiny and dialogue.
